column1: Dear Customer, your DBS bank account has been temporarily suspended due to unusual activity. Verify your account immediately at https://secure-dbs-verify-login.com to avoid permanent suspension.
column8: This message appears likely to be a Banking Scam. It claims your DBS bank account has been suspended due to 'unusual activity' and urges immediate verification through a provided link. Scammers frequently use such tactics, impersonating banks to create a false sense of urgency and trick individuals into revealing sensitive banking information through fake websites. The presence of keywords like 'account', 'bank', 'unusual', and 'immediately' also contributed to this assessment.
column9: The message creates a high sense of urgency about an 'unusual activity' and 'temporary suspension' of your bank account, demanding immediate action to 'verify' it. It includes a suspicious link, 'https://secure-dbs-verify-login.com', which does not appear to be an official DBS website, a common tactic in banking scams to phish for login credentials.
column10:
The message claims your bank account has been 'temporarily suspended due to unusual activity', which is a common tactic used by scammers to create panic and prompt immediate action.
It contains an urgent call to action, demanding you 'verify your account immediately' to avoid 'permanent suspension', which pressures you to act without careful verification.
The message directs you to a link, 'https://secure-dbs-verify-login.com', which attempts to mimic a legitimate bank domain but is not the official DBS website. This is a tell-tale sign of a phishing attempt designed to steal your login credentials.
column11:
Never click on links in unsolicited messages claiming to be from your bank, especially if they warn about account suspension or unusual activity.
Always verify any suspicious messages directly with your bank using their official customer service hotline or through their official banking app/website, not by using contact details or links provided in the suspicious message.
Be extremely cautious of any communication that pressures you to take immediate action or asks for sensitive information like passwords, PINs, or One-Time Passwords (OTPs).
column12:
Stop communicating with the sender of this message immediately and do not click on the provided link or provide any personal information.
Contact DBS Bank directly using their official hotline (found on their official website or the back of your bank card) to inquire about your account status.
Monitor your bank accounts closely for any unauthorised transactions. If you suspect your credentials may have been compromised, contact your bank to freeze or temporarily suspend affected accounts/cards and change your online banking passwords.
column13:
Always access your online banking services through official banking applications or by typing the bank's official website address directly into your browser.
Never share your passwords, PINs, or OTPs with anyone, even if they claim to be from your bank or a trusted authority.
Enable multi-factor authentication and transaction notifications for your banking accounts whenever available to add an extra layer of security.

column1: Congratulations! You have been selected for a remote data entry position earning SGD 5,000 per month. No experience is required. Register now at https://easy-work-from-home-jobs.net to secure your position.
column8: This message appears likely to be a job scam, showing characteristics associated with fraudulent recruitment schemes. The unsolicited 'Congratulations!' for a 'remote data entry position' offering an unusually high 'SGD 5,000 per month' with 'No experience is required' is a significant red flag. These elements, including 'position', 'remote', 'experience', 'register', and 'congratulations', were identified as top contributing keywords by our analysis, aligning with common scam tactics where scammers advertise fake vacancies with unrealistic salaries and minimal requirements to entice victims. The instruction to 'Register now' on an unfamiliar website is also consistent with scam attempts to gather personal information or request payments.
column9: The message exhibits several suspicious characteristics typical of job scams. It begins with an unsolicited 'Congratulations!' for a job you likely didn't apply for, offering an exceptionally high salary of SGD 5,000 per month for a 'remote data entry position' that requires 'No experience'. This promise of high income for minimal effort is a classic scam tactic, as legitimate employers rarely offer such terms without prior application or rigorous assessment. Furthermore, the urgent call to 'Register now' at an unofficial-looking domain, 'https://easy-work-from-home-jobs.net', is a common method for scammers to collect personal data or trick victims into making upfront payments. These elements are strongly consistent with patterns identified by ScamSense for job scams.
column10:
Unsolicited 'Congratulations!' for a job offer you did not apply for.
Promise of high income (SGD 5,000 per month) for a 'remote data entry position' with 'No experience required'.
Urgent request to 'Register now' on an unofficial-looking website (https://easy-work-from-home-jobs.net) to secure a position.
column11:
Be extremely cautious of unsolicited job offers, especially those promising high salaries for minimal effort or experience.
Always verify job offers and company details through official channels, never relying solely on information provided in the suspicious message.
Never pay any fees, such as for registration, training, or equipment, to secure a job opportunity.
column12:
Do not click on any links in the message, particularly the registration link, as it may lead to phishing sites or malware.
Do not reply to the message or share any personal, financial, or identification details with the sender.
Block the sender and report the message to the relevant authorities, such as the Singapore Police Force (SPF) or through platforms like ScamShield.
column13:
Always apply for jobs through official company websites or reputable job portals that you trust.
Research any company thoroughly before accepting an offer, checking their official online presence and reviews.
Be wary of offers that bypass formal interview processes or require immediate commitment without proper assessment.

column1: Your parcel delivery was unsuccessful because the shipping address is incomplete. Please pay a redelivery fee of SGD 2.99 at https://sgparcel-redelivery.com within 24 hours to receive your package.
column8: The message you received appears likely to be a **Parcel Scam** with a high risk level. Scammers often send fake delivery notifications, claiming issues like an incomplete address, to trick you into paying a small fee or clicking malicious links. The request for a 'redelivery fee' and the suspicious link provided are common tactics used in these scams.
column9: The message attempts to create urgency by stating a 24-hour deadline and prompts you to pay a 'redelivery fee' for an 'incomplete shipping address' through a non-official-looking website (`sgparcel-redelivery.com`). This is consistent with common parcel scam patterns where scammers impersonate courier companies to solicit small payments. Legitimate courier companies typically use official channels for such notifications and would not request payment via a generic, unfamiliar link for redelivery issues.
column10:
Unexpected notification about an 'unsuccessful delivery' due to an 'incomplete shipping address'.
Request for a 'redelivery fee' (SGD 2.99) via an external, unfamiliar link.
Presence of a suspicious website link (`https://sgparcel-redelivery.com`) that is unlikely to belong to an official courier service.
Implied urgency with a 'within 24 hours' deadline to receive the package, pressuring you to act quickly.
column11:
Do not click on the link provided in the message or download any attachments.
Avoid making any payments or providing personal information, especially banking credentials, through unexpected links.
Always verify delivery notifications directly with the courier company using their official website or app, not through links in suspicious messages.
column12:
Delete the suspicious message immediately to avoid accidental interaction.
If you have already clicked the link or provided details, contact your bank immediately to monitor your accounts for suspicious activity.
Preserve the message as evidence and consider reporting it to relevant authorities like ScamShield where appropriate.
column13:
Verify parcel notifications by checking your recent purchases and expected deliveries directly with the retailer or courier.
Track parcels only through the courier company's official website or mobile application, not through links in unsolicited messages.
Be cautious of requests for unexpected delivery fees, customs duties, or taxes, which are common in parcel scams.
